category: Continuous, discrete, discontinuities, signal attributes & lookup blocks (extended)
description: Remaining blocks of the Continuous, Discrete, Additional Math & Discrete, Discontinuities, Signal Attributes and Lookup Tables libraries: limited and second-order integrators, 2DOF PID, delays and FIR filters, first-order transfer-function forms, fixed-point counters, dynamic saturation/dead-zone/rate limiters, data-type propagation helpers, and dynamic lookup.

tools.name: Integrator Limited
tools.description: Continuous-time Integrator pre-configured with output saturation limits, so the state stops integrating (anti-windup) when it reaches the upper or lower limit. Use it for actuator position models and PI integrators that must not wind up.
tools.usage:
simulink/Continuous/Integrator Limited
Parameters: LimitOutput ('on'), UpperSaturationLimit, LowerSaturationLimit, InitialCondition, ExternalReset, ShowSaturationPort, ShowStatePort

parameters.name: UpperSaturationLimit / LowerSaturationLimit
parameters.description: Output limits; the state is clamped and integration stops in the saturating direction.

parameters.name: InitialCondition
parameters.description: Initial state value (internal) or supplied through a port with InitialConditionSource 'external'.

parameters.name: ExternalReset
parameters.description: 'none' | 'rising' | 'falling' | 'either' | 'level' | 'level hold' reset trigger port.

parameters.name: ShowSaturationPort
parameters.description: Adds an output indicating -1/0/+1 saturation status.

tools.notes: Same block type as Integrator with LimitOutput on. Limits are tunable only if not inlined.

tools.name: Second-Order Integrator
tools.description: Integrates the input twice in one block, exposing both x (position) and dx/dt (velocity) as outputs with independent initial conditions, limits and reset. Use it for rigid-body translational or rotational motion where you need consistent limiting of both position and velocity (e.g. a mass hitting a stop).
tools.usage:
simulink/Continuous/Second-Order Integrator
Parameters: ICX, ICDXDT, LimitX, UpperLimitX, LowerLimitX, LimitDXDT, UpperLimitDXDT, LowerLimitDXDT, ExternalReset, ReinitDXDTwhenXreachesSaturation

parameters.name: ICX / ICDXDT
parameters.description: Initial conditions for x and dx/dt.

parameters.name: LimitX / LimitDXDT
parameters.description: Enable saturation of x and dx/dt with the corresponding Upper/Lower limits.

parameters.name: ReinitDXDTwhenXreachesSaturation
parameters.description: Reset dx/dt to its initial condition when x saturates (models an inelastic stop).

tools.notes: Second-Order Integrator Limited is the same block with limits enabled. Requires a continuous solver.

tools.name: PID Controller (2DOF)
tools.description: Two-degree-of-freedom PID controller with separate set-point weights b and c on the proportional and derivative paths, so set-point changes and disturbance rejection can be tuned independently. Supports continuous or discrete time, parallel/ideal forms, anti-windup, output saturation, tracking mode and PID Tuner integration.
tools.usage:
simulink/Continuous/PID Controller (2DOF)
Ports: Ref, y (measurement). Parameters: Controller ('PID'|'PI'|'PD'|'P'|'I'), TimeDomain ('Continuous-time'|'Discrete-time'), P, I, D, N, b, c, Form ('Parallel'|'Ideal'), AntiWindupMode, LimitOutput, UpperSaturationLimit, LowerSaturationLimit, TrackingMode, InitialConditionForIntegrator

parameters.name: P, I, D, N
parameters.description: Gains and derivative filter coefficient.

parameters.name: b, c
parameters.description: Set-point weights on the proportional and derivative terms (0..1).

parameters.name: AntiWindupMode
parameters.description: 'none' | 'back-calculation' | 'clamping'.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Sample time for discrete-time controllers.

tools.notes: Click Tune to open PID Tuner (Simulink Control Design). Discrete PID Controller (2DOF) in the Discrete library is the same block with TimeDomain preset.

tools.name: Variable Time Delay
tools.description: Delays the input by a time given on a second input port, interpolating the stored history to produce the delayed value, without treating the delay as a transport (pipe) delay. Use it for time-varying communication or sensor latencies.
tools.usage:
simulink/Continuous/Variable Time Delay
Parameters: VariableDelayType ('Variable time delay'), MaximumDelay, InitialOutput, MaximumPoints (buffer size), FixedBuffer, Order (Pade order for linearization)

parameters.name: MaximumDelay
parameters.description: Upper bound on the delay input; larger values are clipped.

parameters.name: InitialOutput
parameters.description: Output before the first delayed sample is available.

parameters.name: MaximumPoints / FixedBuffer
parameters.description: Size of the history buffer used to store past inputs.

tools.notes: Variable Transport Delay is the same block with VariableDelayType set to 'Variable transport delay' (models fluid/conveyor transport). Requires a continuous solver.

tools.name: Descriptor State-Space
tools.description: Models a linear implicit (descriptor) system E*dx/dt = A*x + B*u, y = C*x + D*u, including singular E (differential-algebraic systems). Use it for systems returned by dss or extracted from Simscape/mechanical models with algebraic constraints; choose daessc or ode15s/ode23t solvers.
tools.usage:
simulink/Continuous/Descriptor State-Space
Parameters: E, A, B, C, D, InitialCondition, DirectFeedthrough, AbsTol, MaxOrder (differential index handling)

parameters.name: E, A, B, C, D
parameters.description: Descriptor system matrices; E may be singular.

parameters.name: InitialCondition
parameters.description: Initial state x0 (must be consistent with the algebraic constraints).

tools.notes: Index-1 systems are supported directly; higher-index systems must be reduced. Linearization with linmod/linearize is supported.

tools.name: First Order Hold
tools.description: Converts a discrete-time input into a continuous piecewise-linear signal by linearly interpolating between samples (a first-order hold reconstruction), as opposed to the staircase of Zero-Order Hold. Use it in mixed-signal models to approximate a smoother D/A reconstruction.
tools.usage:
simulink/Continuous/First Order Hold
Parameters: SampleTime? (inherits from input), InitialOutput

parameters.name: InitialOutput
parameters.description: Output value before the second sample is available.

tools.notes: Introduces a one-sample delay because interpolation needs the next sample. Requires a continuous solver.

tools.name: Discrete FIR Filter
tools.description: Implements a finite-impulse-response filter with coefficients from the dialog or an input port, using direct form, symmetric/antisymmetric, lattice MA or transposed structures with full fixed-point control. Use it for moving averages, decimation prefilters and any tap-based filtering that must generate efficient code.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Discrete FIR Filter
Parameters: CoefSource ('Dialog parameters'|'Input port'), Coefficients, FilterStructure ('Direct form'|'Direct form symmetric'|'Direct form antisymmetric'|'Direct form transposed'|'Lattice MA'), InitialStates, SampleTime, InputProcessing ('Columns as channels (frame based)'|'Elements as channels (sample based)'), CoefDataTypeStr, ProductDataTypeStr, AccumDataTypeStr, OutDataTypeStr

parameters.name: Coefficients
parameters.description: Row vector of FIR taps, e.g. fir1(20,0.2) or ones(1,8)/8.

parameters.name: FilterStructure
parameters.description: Realization; symmetric forms halve the multiplies for linear-phase filters.

parameters.name: InputProcessing
parameters.description: Frame-based (columns) or sample-based (elements) channel interpretation.

parameters.name: InitialStates
parameters.description: Initial filter memory.

tools.notes: For IIR filters use Discrete Filter (numerator/denominator) or Discrete Transfer Fcn. DSP System Toolbox adds Biquad Filter and FIR Decimation with optimized structures.

tools.name: Discrete Zero-Pole
tools.description: Implements a discrete transfer function specified by its zeros, poles and gain in the z-domain. Use it when the design is naturally expressed in pole-zero form (e.g. from zpk) rather than polynomial coefficients.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Discrete Zero-Pole
Parameters: Zeros, Poles, Gain, SampleTime

parameters.name: Zeros / Poles
parameters.description: Vectors of z-plane zeros and poles (complex pairs allowed); number of poles must be >= number of zeros.

parameters.name: Gain
parameters.description: Scalar gain K.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Discrete sample time or -1 to inherit.

tools.notes: Zero-Pole is the continuous counterpart. The block does not support fixed-point; use Discrete Filter for that.

tools.name: Tapped Delay
tools.description: Delays a scalar input by 1..N samples and outputs all N delayed values as a vector (optionally including the current input), i.e. a delay line. Use it to build FIR structures, sliding windows and history buffers for MATLAB Function blocks.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Tapped Delay
Parameters: NumDelays, vinit (Initial condition), DelayOrder ('Oldest'|'Newest'), includeCurrent ('on' adds u(k) to the vector), samptime

parameters.name: NumDelays
parameters.description: Number of taps N; output width is N (or N+1 with includeCurrent).

parameters.name: DelayOrder
parameters.description: Whether the oldest or newest sample comes first in the output vector.

parameters.name: vinit
parameters.description: Initial content of the delay line.

tools.notes: Input must be scalar per channel; for vector histories use Delay with a Buffer (DSP System Toolbox).

tools.name: Discrete Derivative
tools.description: Computes K*(u(k) - u(k-1))/Ts, the first-difference approximation of the derivative scaled by the sample time. Use it for discrete rate calculations that must remain correct when Ts changes; it supports fixed-point data types.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Discrete Derivative
Parameters: gainval (K), ICPrevScaledInput (initial condition for the previous input), OutDataTypeStr

parameters.name: gainval
parameters.description: Gain K multiplying the difference quotient.

parameters.name: ICPrevScaledInput
parameters.description: Initial value of the previous scaled input.

tools.notes: Amplifies noise like any differentiator; consider a filtered derivative (Discrete PID D term with N) instead. Difference gives u(k)-u(k-1) without dividing by Ts.

tools.name: Difference
tools.description: Outputs u(k) - u(k-1), the change of the input since the previous sample, with fixed-point support. Use it to detect steps or compute increments without the 1/Ts scaling of Discrete Derivative.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Difference
Parameters: vinit (Initial condition for previous output), OutDataTypeStr, RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: vinit
parameters.description: Initial previous input value.

tools.notes: Masked subsystem built from Unit Delay and Sum; inherits sample time from the input.

tools.name: Resettable Delay
tools.description: Delay block pre-configured with an external reset port that reinitializes the delay buffer to its initial condition on a rising, falling or either edge (or level). Use it for restartable pipelines and filters that must forget history on an event.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Resettable Delay
Parameters: DelayLength, InitialCondition, ExternalReset ('Rising'|'Falling'|'Either'|'Level'|'Level hold'), ShowEnablePort, SampleTime, DelayLengthSource ('Dialog'|'Input port'), DelayLengthUpperLimit

parameters.name: DelayLength
parameters.description: Number of samples to delay (dialog) or maximum when supplied by port.

parameters.name: ExternalReset
parameters.description: Edge/level type of the reset input.

parameters.name: InitialCondition
parameters.description: Value(s) loaded into the buffer at start and on reset.

tools.notes: It is the Delay block with ExternalReset set; enabling ShowEnablePort gives an Enabled Delay as well.

tools.name: Variable Integer Delay
tools.description: Delay block whose delay length in samples is set at run time by an input port, bounded by an upper limit. Use it for programmable latency, adaptive equalizers and buffer alignment.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Variable Integer Delay
Parameters: DelayLengthSource ('Input port'), DelayLengthUpperLimit, InitialCondition, SampleTime, ExternalReset, ShowEnablePort

parameters.name: DelayLengthUpperLimit
parameters.description: Maximum delay; the buffer is sized to this value and larger inputs are clipped.

parameters.name: InitialCondition
parameters.description: Initial buffer contents.

tools.notes: The delay input must be an integer-valued signal; use Data Type Conversion with floor if needed.

tools.name: Transfer Fcn First Order
tools.description: Discrete first-order low-pass filter y(k) = (1-p)*u(k) + p*y(k-1), parameterized by the pole location, with fixed-point support. Use it as a lightweight smoothing filter in embedded controllers.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Transfer Fcn First Order
Parameters: PoleZ (pole location 0..1), ICPrevOutput (initial condition of previous output), RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: PoleZ
parameters.description: z-plane pole; closer to 1 means heavier filtering.

parameters.name: ICPrevOutput
parameters.description: Initial previous output.

tools.notes: DC gain is 1. Related: Transfer Fcn Lead or Lag, Transfer Fcn Real Zero.

tools.name: Transfer Fcn Lead or Lag
tools.description: Discrete lead or lag compensator (z - z0)/(z - p0) with unity DC gain, parameterized by a pole and a zero, supporting fixed-point. Use it for phase-lead/lag compensation in embedded loops.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Transfer Fcn Lead or Lag
Parameters: PoleZ, ZeroZ, ICPrevOutput, ICPrevInput, RndMeth

parameters.name: PoleZ / ZeroZ
parameters.description: z-plane pole and zero (0..1); zero < pole gives lag, zero > pole gives lead.

parameters.name: ICPrevOutput / ICPrevInput
parameters.description: Initial conditions of previous output and input.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Discrete/Transfer Fcn Lead or Lag', 'm/Lead');
set_param('m/Lead', 'PoleZ', '0.5', 'ZeroZ', '0.8');
tools.notes: The block normalizes for unity steady-state gain, unlike a raw Discrete Transfer Fcn.

tools.name: Transfer Fcn Real Zero
tools.description: Discrete transfer function with a single real zero and no poles, y(k) = u(k) - z0*u(k-1) normalized for unity DC gain, with fixed-point support. Use it as a simple differentiating/pre-emphasis element.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Transfer Fcn Real Zero
Parameters: ZeroZ, ICPrevInput, RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: ZeroZ
parameters.description: z-plane zero location.

parameters.name: ICPrevInput
parameters.description: Initial previous input.

tools.notes: Part of the fixed-point discrete transfer-function family with Transfer Fcn First Order and Lead or Lag.

tools.name: Discrete PID Controller (2DOF)
tools.description: Discrete-time version of the two-degree-of-freedom PID Controller with set-point weights b and c, selectable integrator and filter methods (Forward Euler, Backward Euler, Trapezoidal), anti-windup and saturation. Use it in sampled controllers destined for code generation.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discrete/Discrete PID Controller (2DOF)
Parameters: Controller, P, I, D, N, b, c, IntegratorMethod, FilterMethod, SampleTime, AntiWindupMode, LimitOutput, UpperSaturationLimit, LowerSaturationLimit

parameters.name: IntegratorMethod / FilterMethod
parameters.description: 'Forward Euler' | 'Backward Euler' | 'Trapezoidal' discretization of I and D terms.

parameters.name: SampleTime
parameters.description: Controller sample time (-1 inherits).

parameters.name: b, c
parameters.description: Set-point weights for the P and D paths.

tools.notes: Same block as PID Controller (2DOF) with TimeDomain 'Discrete-time'. Supports fixed-point via the Data Types tab.

tools.name: Fixed-Point State-Space
tools.description: Discrete state-space system x(k+1) = A x + B u, y = C x + D u implemented with explicit fixed-point data types for states, internal products and outputs. Use it for embedded observers and controllers when the standard Discrete State-Space block's floating-point-only restriction is a problem.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Discrete/Fixed-Point State-Space
Parameters: A, B, C, D, InitialCondition (initial state), DataTypeForInternalCalculations, ScalingForInternalCalc, DataTypeForOutput, ScalingForOutput, RndMeth

parameters.name: A, B, C, D
parameters.description: State-space matrices.

parameters.name: DataTypeForInternalCalculations / ScalingForInternalCalc
parameters.description: Fixed-point type and scaling for states and intermediate products.

parameters.name: DataTypeForOutput / ScalingForOutput
parameters.description: Output data type and scaling.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Discrete/Fixed-Point State-Space', 'm/FxSS');
set_param('m/FxSS', 'A', 'Ad', 'B', 'Bd', 'C', 'Cd', 'D', 'Dd');
tools.notes: Masked block built from Delay, Gain and Sum blocks; the Fixed-Point Tool can propose the scalings.

tools.name: Transfer Fcn Direct Form II
tools.description: Implements a discrete IIR transfer function in canonical Direct Form II with explicit fixed-point control over the intermediate state, using numerator and denominator coefficient vectors. Use it when you need a fixed-point IIR filter with the minimum number of delay elements.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Discrete/Transfer Fcn Direct Form II
Parameters: NumCoefVec, DenCoefVec (leading coefficient 1 assumed), vinit (initial states), RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: NumCoefVec / DenCoefVec
parameters.description: Numerator and denominator coefficients in descending powers of z^-1 (denominator excluding the leading 1).

parameters.name: vinit
parameters.description: Initial condition of the internal states.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Discrete/Transfer Fcn Direct Form II', 'm/DF2');
set_param('m/DF2', 'NumCoefVec', '[0.2 0.3 0.2]', 'DenCoefVec', '[-0.9 0.4]');
tools.notes: Direct Form II can overflow internally with high-gain filters; scale coefficients or choose a wider internal type. Time-varying coefficients: use Transfer Fcn Direct Form II Time Varying.

tools.name: Transfer Fcn Direct Form II Time Varying
tools.description: Direct Form II IIR filter whose numerator and denominator coefficients are supplied as input signals every sample, so the filter can be adapted on the fly. Use it for adaptive filters and gain-scheduled digital compensators.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Discrete/Transfer Fcn Direct Form II Time Varying
Ports: u, Num, Den. Parameters: vinit, RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: Num / Den ports
parameters.description: Coefficient vectors as signals; Den excludes the leading 1.

parameters.name: vinit
parameters.description: Initial internal states.

tools.example: add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Discrete/Transfer Fcn Direct Form II Time Varying', 'm/DF2TV');
tools.notes: The coefficient port widths fix the filter order at compile time.

tools.name: Increment Real World
tools.description: Adds 1 to the real-world value of the input signal, so for a fixed-point signal the stored integer changes by 1/slope. Use it for counters expressed in engineering units; wraps or saturates per the model overflow setting.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Increment Real World
No dialog parameters.
tools.example: add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Increment Real World', 'm/IncRW');
tools.notes: Output data type equals the input type. Related: Increment Stored Integer (adds 1 to the raw integer), Decrement Real World.

tools.name: Decrement Real World
tools.description: Subtracts 1 from the real-world value of the input signal, preserving the data type. Use it for countdowns in engineering units.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Real World
No dialog parameters.
tools.example: add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Real World', 'm/DecRW');
tools.notes: Related: Decrement To Zero (stops at 0), Decrement Time To Zero (subtracts the sample time instead of 1).

tools.name: Increment Stored Integer
tools.description: Adds 1 to the stored integer value of a fixed-point or integer input, ignoring slope and bias, i.e. the raw bit pattern is incremented. Use it for bit-exact counters and array indices in fixed-point designs.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Increment Stored Integer
No dialog parameters.
tools.example: add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Increment Stored Integer', 'm/IncSI');
tools.notes: For a fixdt(1,16,4) signal the real-world value increases by 2^-4. Floating-point inputs behave like Increment Real World.

tools.name: Decrement Stored Integer
tools.description: Subtracts 1 from the stored integer value of a fixed-point or integer input, ignoring scaling. Use it with Increment Stored Integer for raw counters.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Stored Integer
No dialog parameters.
tools.example: add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Stored Integer', 'm/DecSI');
tools.notes: Overflow behaviour follows the input type (wrap for stored-integer arithmetic).

tools.name: Decrement To Zero
tools.description: Decrements the input real-world value by 1 but never below zero, saturating at 0. Use it for down-counters and timers that must stop at zero.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement To Zero
No dialog parameters.
tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement To Zero', 'm/DecZ');
% feed back through a Unit Delay to make a countdown timer
tools.notes: Decrement Time To Zero subtracts the block sample time instead of 1, giving a countdown in seconds.

tools.name: Decrement Time To Zero
tools.description: Subtracts the block's sample time from the input each step, saturating at zero, producing a countdown in seconds that remains correct when the sample time changes. Use it for time-out timers in discrete logic.
tools.usage:
simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Time To Zero
No dialog parameters (sample time inherited).
tools.example: add_block('simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Time To Zero', 'm/Timer');
tools.notes: Must inherit a discrete sample time. Stateflow after(n, sec) is a more readable alternative for timeouts inside charts.

tools.name: Saturation Dynamic
tools.description: Limits the input u between the values supplied on the lo and up input ports, so the saturation bounds can vary at run time. Use it for actuator limits that depend on operating conditions (e.g. torque limits versus speed).
tools.usage:
simulink/Discontinuities/Saturation Dynamic
Ports: up, u, lo. Parameters: OutDataTypeStr, RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Output data type (inherit or explicit).

tools.notes: Masked subsystem using MinMax/Switch blocks; no zero-crossing detection. Static bounds: Saturation block.

tools.name: Dead Zone Dynamic
tools.description: Outputs zero while the input lies between the lo and up port values and passes the excess beyond the bounds otherwise, with run-time adjustable dead band. Use it for adaptive dead bands in actuator models or control error shaping.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discontinuities/Dead Zone Dynamic
Ports: up, u, lo. No dialog parameters.
tools.notes: Static version: Dead Zone. Output = u - up when u > up, u - lo when u < lo, else 0.

tools.name: Rate Limiter Dynamic
tools.description: Limits the rate of change of the input using rising and falling slew rates supplied on input ports, evaluated per sample. Use it for slew-rate limits that depend on state, such as ramp rates that vary with gear or temperature.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discontinuities/Rate Limiter Dynamic
Ports: up (rising rate), u, lo (falling rate, negative). Parameters: initial condition via mask (Ic)

parameters.name: up / lo ports
parameters.description: Maximum positive and negative rates in units per second.

tools.notes: Discrete implementation; inherits the sample time of the input. Static rates: Rate Limiter.

tools.name: Coulomb and Viscous Friction
tools.description: Models friction as a Coulomb offset (sign(u)*offset) plus a viscous term proportional to the input, y = sign(u).*(gain.*abs(u) + offset), with a discontinuity at zero. Use it in mechanical drive models for stick-slip-free friction torque.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discontinuities/Coulomb and Viscous Friction
Parameters: offset (Coulomb friction value), gain (viscous coefficient)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Coulomb friction magnitude applied with the sign of the input (may be a vector).

parameters.name: gain
parameters.description: Viscous friction coefficient.

tools.notes: The discontinuity at zero speed can cause chattering with variable-step solvers; consider a Simscape friction block for physically consistent stiction.

tools.name: Wrap To Zero
tools.description: Outputs zero when the input exceeds a threshold and passes the input through otherwise. Use it to implement modulo-like counters that restart when reaching a limit, especially with fixed-point counters.
tools.usage:
simulink/Discontinuities/Wrap To Zero
Parameters: Threshold

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: Value above which the output is forced to zero.

tools.notes: Output data type equals input type. For true modulo arithmetic use Math Function with 'mod' or 'rem'.

tools.name: Data Type Conversion Inherited
tools.description: Converts the first input to the data type of the second (reference) input, so the target type is inherited from another signal instead of being typed into a dialog. Use it in library blocks and reusable subsystems that must adapt to whatever type the surrounding model uses.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Data Type Conversion Inherited
Ports: u (signal), (reference type). Parameters: ConvertRealWorld ('Real World Value (RWV)'|'Stored Integer (SI)'), RndMeth, SaturateOnIntegerOverflow

parameters.name: ConvertRealWorld
parameters.description: Preserve real-world value (rescale) or stored integer bits.

parameters.name: RndMeth
parameters.description: Rounding mode for fixed-point conversion.

tools.notes: Related: Data Type Conversion (explicit type), Data Type Duplicate (forces equality without conversion).

tools.name: Data Type Duplicate
tools.description: Forces all connected signals to have the same data type by back-propagating a single inherited type to all its input ports; it has no output. Use it in masked library blocks so that, e.g., a parameter constant takes the same type as the signal it is compared with.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Data Type Duplicate
Parameters: NumInputPorts

parameters.name: NumInputPorts
parameters.description: Number of signals to bind to one data type.

tools.notes: Errors if the connected signals resolve to different explicit types. Purely compile-time; no code is generated.

tools.name: Data Type Propagation
tools.description: Sets the data type and scaling of a reference signal (Prop port) as a function of the data types of two other reference signals (Ref1, Ref2), using rules for signedness, word length, slope and bias. Use it inside fixed-point library blocks to derive intermediate types (e.g. accumulator width = max of inputs + 1).
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Data Type Propagation
Ports: Ref1, Ref2, Prop. Parameters: PropDataTypeMode, PropDataType, IfRefDouble, IfRefSingle, IsSigned, NumBitsBase, NumBitsMult, NumBitsAdd, NumBitsAllowFinal, PropScalingMode, PropScaling, ValuesUsedBestPrec, NumBitsBias..., ExtraBits

parameters.name: PropDataTypeMode
parameters.description: 'Specify via dialog' or 'Inherit via propagation rule'.

parameters.name: IsSigned / NumBitsBase / NumBitsMult / NumBitsAdd
parameters.description: Rules building the propagated word length from Ref1/Ref2 (max, min, sum...).

parameters.name: PropScalingMode
parameters.description: Slope/bias or best-precision rule for the propagated scaling.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Attributes/Data Type Propagation', 'm/DTProp');
set_param('m/DTProp', 'NumBitsBase', 'max([WL1 WL2])', 'NumBitsAdd', '1');
tools.notes: Requires Fixed-Point Designer for fixed-point rules. Related: Data Type Scaling Strip.

tools.name: Data Type Scaling Strip
tools.description: Removes the slope and bias of a fixed-point input, outputting the stored integer as a plain integer of the same word length and signedness. Use it before bit-manipulation or communication packing where raw integers are required.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Data Type Scaling Strip
No dialog parameters.
tools.notes: Floating-point inputs pass through unchanged. Inverse operation: Data Type Conversion in 'Stored Integer' mode.

tools.name: Width
tools.description: Outputs the number of elements (width) of its input signal as a constant, with a selectable output data type. Use it in masks and scalable subsystems to size other computations from the connected signal.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Width
Parameters: OutputDataTypeScalingMode ('Choose intrinsic data type'|'Inherit via back propagation'|'All ports same datatype'), DataType

parameters.name: DataType
parameters.description: Output type such as 'double', 'int32'.

tools.notes: For matrices the output is the total element count. Value is fixed at compile time.

tools.name: Probe
tools.description: Outputs selected attributes of the input signal - width, sample time [period offset], complexity, dimensions and signal type - as separate output ports, without altering the signal. Use it for diagnostics and for feeding attribute-dependent logic.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Probe
Parameters: ProbeWidth, ProbeSampleTime, ProbeComplexSignal, ProbeSignalDimensions, ProbeFramedSignal, ProbeWidthDataType, ProbeSampleTimeDataType, ...

parameters.name: ProbeWidth / ProbeSampleTime / ProbeComplexSignal / ProbeSignalDimensions
parameters.description: 'on' adds an output port for that attribute.

tools.notes: Attribute outputs are constants determined at compile time.

tools.name: Signal Conversion
tools.description: Converts between signal storage forms: contiguous copy of a virtual (muxed) signal, virtual bus to nonvirtual bus, or nonvirtual to virtual bus. Use it to satisfy blocks that require a nonvirtual bus (e.g. model reference ports, S-functions) or to force a contiguous copy for code generation.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Signal Conversion
Parameters: ConversionOutput ('Signal copy' | 'Virtual bus' | 'Nonvirtual bus'), OutDataTypeStr ('Bus: MyBus' for nonvirtual), OverrideOpt

parameters.name: ConversionOutput
parameters.description: Target form of the output signal.

parameters.name: OutDataTypeStr
parameters.description: Simulink.Bus object name when producing a nonvirtual bus.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Attributes/Signal Conversion', 'm/ToNVBus');
set_param('m/ToNVBus', 'ConversionOutput', 'Nonvirtual bus', 'OutDataTypeStr', 'Bus: SensorBus');
tools.notes: Bus to Vector is the dedicated block for converting a virtual bus of like elements into a vector.

tools.name: IC
tools.description: Sets the initial value of a signal at the first time step (and optionally at the start of every step of an enabled subsystem execution) and passes the input through afterwards. Use it to break algebraic loops or to provide a defined value to feedback paths before the first computation.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/IC
Parameters: Value (initial value), SampleTime

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Value output at t = start; must match the input dimensions.

tools.notes: Does not break an algebraic loop for continuous signals by itself; use a Memory or Unit Delay. Inside conditionally executed subsystems the IC applies at each re-enable when the subsystem states reset.

tools.name: Unit Conversion
tools.description: Converts the input to a specified output unit (e.g. 'deg' to 'rad', 'km/h' to 'm/s') using the Simulink unit database, so unit inconsistencies between components are handled explicitly. Use it at interfaces between models authored in different unit systems.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Unit Conversion
Parameters: Unit (output unit string, e.g. 'm/s'), OutDataTypeStr

parameters.name: Unit
parameters.description: Target unit; input unit is taken from the signal's propagated unit.

tools.notes: Requires units to be specified on upstream ports (Inport/Signal Specification Unit parameter). See Unit System Configuration to restrict allowed unit systems.

tools.name: Bus to Vector
tools.description: Converts a virtual bus whose elements have identical attributes (type, dimensions, complexity) into a plain vector signal, making an implicit bus-as-vector usage explicit. Use it when a block that expects a vector (Gain, Mux downstream) is connected to a bus; Simulink.BlockDiagram.addBusToVector inserts these blocks automatically.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Bus to Vector
No dialog parameters.
tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Attributes/Bus to Vector', 'm/B2V');
% or: Simulink.BlockDiagram.addBusToVector('m', true)
tools.notes: Nonvirtual buses cannot be converted; use Bus Selector or Signal Conversion. The diagnostic 'Bus signal treated as vector' (StrictBusMsg) governs implicit conversions.

tools.name: Weighted Sample Time
tools.description: Outputs the input multiplied, divided, added or subtracted with the weighted sample time w*Ts, or outputs Ts or 1/Ts alone, exactly like Weighted Sample Time Math but located in the Signal Attributes library. Use it to expose the sample time as a signal for logging or for sample-time-aware arithmetic.
tools.usage:
simulink/Signal Attributes/Weighted Sample Time
Parameters: TsampMathOp ('+' | '-' | '*' | '/' | 'Ts Only' | '1/Ts Only'), weightValue, TsampMathImp, OutDataTypeStr

parameters.name: TsampMathOp
parameters.description: Operation with the weighted sample time.

parameters.name: weightValue
parameters.description: Weight w.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Signal Attributes/Weighted Sample Time', 'm/TsOut');
set_param('m/TsOut', 'TsampMathOp', 'Ts Only');
tools.notes: Same block type as Weighted Sample Time Math (SampleTimeMath).

tools.name: Lookup Table Dynamic
tools.description: One-dimensional lookup whose breakpoint vector (xdat) and table data (ydat) are supplied as input signals, so the table can change during simulation. Use it for calibration maps updated at run time or computed from other signals; supports interpolation, extrapolation and nearest/above/below modes.
tools.usage:
simulink/Lookup Tables/Lookup Table Dynamic
Ports: x, xdat, ydat. Parameters: LookUpMeth ('Interpolation-Extrapolation' | 'Interpolation-Use End Values' | 'Use Input Nearest' | 'Use Input Below' | 'Use Input Above'), OutDataTypeStr, RndMeth

parameters.name: LookUpMeth
parameters.description: Interpolation/extrapolation behaviour.

parameters.name: xdat / ydat ports
parameters.description: Breakpoint vector (must be increasing) and table values with matching length.

tools.example:
add_block('simulink/Lookup Tables/Lookup Table Dynamic', 'm/LUTdyn');
set_param('m/LUTdyn', 'LookUpMeth', 'Interpolation-Use End Values');
tools.notes: Only 1-D; for static tables 1-D Lookup Table generates more efficient code. Breakpoints must be sorted; the block does not check monotonicity at run time.

tools.name: Sine
tools.description: Lookup-table implementation of sin (and, in the Cosine variant, cos) for fixed-point inputs in revolutions (0..1 scaled), using a quarter-wave table with a configurable number of data points. Use it in embedded designs where trigonometric functions must be computed without floating point.
tools.usage:
simulink/Lookup Tables/Sine  (and Cosine)
Parameters: Formula ('sin(2*pi*u)' | 'cos(2*pi*u)' | 'exp(j*2*pi*u)' | 'sin(2*pi*u) and cos(2*pi*u)'), NumDataPoints (2^n+1), OutputWordLength, InternalRulePriority

parameters.name: Formula
parameters.description: Which function(s) the block evaluates.

parameters.name: NumDataPoints
parameters.description: Table length; larger tables give higher accuracy at more memory.

parameters.name: OutputWordLength
parameters.description: Word length of the fixed-point output.

tools.notes: Input represents the angle as a fraction of a full turn (fixdt(0,16,16) style). Trigonometric Function with CORDIC is the alternative fixed-point approach.
